title: TREND CAPTURE V2 — REGIME PERFORMANCE ANALYSIS
regime_definitions: Using existing system regime classifications from analyzeMarketRegime():

regimes.RANGE: bb_width < 15 (narrow) or bb_width > 40 (wide but not trending)

STRONG_BULL.max_dd: varies, included in total max DD 52.92%
STRONG_BULL.note: Most frequent regime; V2 enters trades but BB position filter applies

BULL.note: Frequent regime; BB position filter applies to all entries

RANGE.note: Challenging regime for trend capture; BB position filter limits entries

STRONG_BEAR.note: Bearish regime; V2 SHORT entries attempted but BB position filter applies

BEAR.note: Bearish regime; similar pattern to STRONG_BEAR

key_insight:
V2 does not gain trend participation by destroying range/chop performance. 
  Range/chop trades (36 RANGE + some chop-adjacent) are limited by the BB position filter
  and anti-FOMO protections (pctB < 80 for LONG, pctB > 20 for SHORT). The strategy's
  structural BB-position blocker applies across ALL regimes without exception.
conclusion:
Regime performance alone does not explain the strategy's underperformance. 
  The dominant structural blocker is the BB position filter, which applies uniformly 
  across ALL regimes without exception. 0/32 strong trend events caught, regardless 
  of whether the regime was trend, range, or high volatility.
